interactions.teaches: Four reasonable fixes can all transfer control in the same direction.
interactions.studentAction: Open each charter row to reveal the problem, rule, and beneficiary.
interactions.feedback: The beneficiary column repeats existing owners or league leadership; after all four rows open, the page names the common direction without assigning a villain score.
interactions.staticFallback: All four rows render open as labeled records when scripts are unavailable or motion is reduced.
interactions.identityFit: The finding emerges from reading a ruled charter ledger rather than a generic quiz.

interactions.teaches: A wage responds to rival bids until owners collectively remove those bids.
interactions.studentAction: Move three rival bids, then apply or remove the reserve list.
interactions.feedback: The wage follows the highest open bid. When reserved, rival controls become inert and the single remaining offer becomes the wage; a permanent label notes that the player had no control in the agreement.
interactions.staticFallback: Open-market and reserved-market states appear side by side in the noscript and print views.
interactions.identityFit: The instrument works as a price column in an owner ledger, making missing competition visible.

interactions.teaches: Pay and freedom to change employers are separate facts.
interactions.studentAction: Reveal five occupations one at a time on a fixed pay-and-freedom field.
interactions.feedback: Each point appears with a short evidence note. The reserved ballplayer lands in the high-pay, low-freedom corner that the other occupations leave nearly empty.
interactions.staticFallback: All five points and their evidence render in a readable list and static plot.
interactions.identityFit: The plot is ruled into the account book and treats placement as an audit finding, not a score.
